mike_support: Heads up — enterprise customer on Vercel Edge is seeing repeated SSE reconnects and early ReadableStream closes when using our TS SDK. They say it started after an automated dependency bump.

mike_support: Env: SDK v1.4.2, edge runtime (Vercel), Node 18 build target, app uses our streaming chat API via the SDK's createStream interface. Symptoms: frequent 401s during streaming, then client side stream closes and SDK retries, leading to many short lived connections and billing spikes.

mike_support: Quick repro they provided (sanitized):
```ts
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-1', messages });
const reader = stream.getReader();
while(true){ const { value, done } = await reader.read(); if(done) break; processChunk(value); }
```
they also showed logs: `FetchError: Unexpected end of ReadableStream` and `401 when refreshing token`

sarah_engineering: Thanks — can you add the exact bundle step they use (build target, bundler) and whether they use cross-fetch/undici polyfills? Also what version of the SDK packages are installed exactly (npm ls).

mike_support: They use Next.js app deployed to Vercel edge, default Vercel bundler, no custom polyfills. npm ls shows `@redwood/sdk@1.4.2`, `cross-fetch@3.1.5`. They confirmed they didn't pin `undici`.

raj_eng: Noted. There's a recent change where the SDK started sending an `x-rdwd-client` header (set by the bundler/ts compiler) and we added a small token refresh handshake that expects streaming fetch to remain open while refresh happens. If the edge runtime's fetch polyfill replaces native stream behavior or strips some headers, the refresh request can 401 and we close the stream. Could be a header/compat mismatch.

raj_eng: Can we get their server logs for token refresh endpoint? If refresh fails with 401 there that's the smoking gun. Also, which retry policy did they configure? Default retries will attempt refresh+reconnect which looks like multiple short streams.

logs-bot: Attached snippet from their logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-10T14:12:02Z ERROR stream-session: token refresh failed status=401 body="invalid_grant"
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z WARN stream-session: closing readable stream due to auth failure
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z INFO sdk: retrying stream connect attempt=1
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z ERROR sdk: fetch error Unexpected end of ReadableStream
```

linh_devex: Repro we tried in-house: Using Next Edge + cross-fetch causes `ReadableStream` to behave differently vs native edge. When cross-fetch is bundled it surfaces a node-style stream wrapper that doesn't support the `getReader()` backpressure semantics. That leads to early `done=true` in some cases especially when auth refresh happens concurrently.

linh_devex: Workarounds: 1) Ensure bundler preserves native streams (in Next: set `experimental: { runtime: 'edge' }` and avoid polyfilling `fetch`), 2) pin SDK to v1.5.0-beta that includes a guard to postpone refresh until stream flush, or 3) opt out of automatic token refresh and handle refresh externally (set `auth: { autoRefresh: false }`).

sarah_engineering: We should prioritize a patch. I'll open a hotfix branch to 1.4.x and backport the guard against closing streams on transient 401 during refresh. Also add a clearer error for `Unexpected end of ReadableStream` when auth refresh fails.

sarah_engineering: Quick patch plan:
- add header check to skip refresh if `x-rdwd-client` missing (possible bundler strip)
- ensure readable stream isn't closed until retry window elapses (200-500ms)
- add telemetry tag `stream_auth_retry`

raj_eng: I can prototype the delay guard. It will hold stream open for one retry attempt and then close if still failing. This reduces churn for short-lived refresh races.

linh_devex: Minimal repro snippet we used (works on local edge emulation):
```ts
// reproduce.js
import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RDW_KEY });
async function run(){
  const s = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-1', messages: [{role:'user',content:'hi'}] });
  const r = s.getReader();
  try{
    while(true){ const {value, done} = await r.read(); if(done) break; console.log('chunk', value); }
  }catch(err){ console.error('stream err', err.message); }
}
run();
```
Note: adding `globalThis.fetch = globalThis.fetch;` hack (noop) sometimes forces native fetch through. Strange bundler effect.

mike_support: Customer asked for a step-by-step workaround they can apply ASAP. I'll pass along: a) pin SDK to `1.5.0-beta` or b) disable auto refresh: `client = createClient({ auth: { autoRefresh: false } })` and do token rotation at app level, c) rebuild without cross-fetch polyfill on Vercel edge.

sarah_engineering: Deploy-bot — can you push the staging hotfix (branch: hotfix/stream-auth-delay) and tag a canary release so dev teams can test?

deploy-bot: Staging deploy triggered for hotfix/stream-auth-delay at 1768123520, canary package `@redwood/sdk@1.4.3-canary.1` published.

logs-bot: Quick telemetry after canary: `stream_auth_retry` events up for edge targets; success rate improved in our internal tests from 78% -> 96% for edge + cross-fetch bundle.

raj_eng: I'll prepare the backport PR to 1.4.x. Also adding a test harness emulating Vercel's bundling to catch regressions.

mike_support: Thanks team — I'll share the canary with the customer, include the two workarounds, and ask for a time window to test. Will update the thread when they confirm. :thumbsup:

sarah_engineering: Followup action list: 1) backport PR, 2) add telemetry + unit tests, 3) create a short doc explaining edge bundler pitfalls and recommended settings (linh, can you draft?).

linh_devex: On it — will draft a 1-pager with quick fixes and a checklist for Next/Vercel edge (headers to preserve, polyfills to avoid).

mike_support: closing note: customer saw significant billing spike due to reconnect storms; flagged as P1 for support billing review. we'll coordinate with finance if credits needed.

sarah_engineering: Noted. Thanks everyone.
